_comment: Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management for the ClipForge bucket.
This is the retention mechanism. There is no cron job and no Cloud Function,
because neither would be better: Google evaluates these rules server-side,
for free, whether or not the worker is running. A scheduled task on the
worker would stop expiring clips during exactly the week the machine is off
and the bucket is growing unattended.
Age is measured from object creation, which for a clip is its upload — so
'5 days after upload' is expressed directly rather than approximated.
Deletion here is silent: nothing tells Firestore that an object has gone.
That is handled without a reconciliation pass by Clip.playbackExpiresAt,
which the worker stamps at upload from CLIPFORGE_CLIP_RETENTION_DAYS. The
two numbers must agree, so tools/storage-lifecycle.ps1 reads that setting
and rewrites the age below before applying this file.
Inspect with: gcloud storage buckets describe gs://BUCKET --format='value(lifecycle)'
